title: Algebraic closure of a field
statement: Let $K$ be a field. A field $\Omega$ is *algebraically closed* if every nonconstant polynomial in $\Omega[X]$ has a root in $\Omega$. An *algebraic closure* of $K$ is an algebraically closed field $\overline K$ together with a field homomorphism $\iota:K\to\overline K$ such that $\overline K$ is algebraic over $K$ (every element of $\overline K$ is a root of a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $\iota(K)$). Every field has an algebraic closure, and any two algebraic closures of $K$ are isomorphic over $K$; 'a fixed algebraic closure' means one chosen once and for all.
